html:
The Xetá are an Indigenous people of the Serra dos Dourados in northwestern Paraná, southern Brazil. They speak a Tupi-Guarani language.

They lived as hunter-gatherers in the forest, using stone axes, until the 1940s and 1950s, when coffee planters and settlers cleared their land. Contact came in the early 1950s, and within a few years most Xetá had died or been scattered, many children being taken away to live with settlers. Only a few survivors remained, and their language is nearly extinct. Their descendants have since gathered to claim land. Neighbours included the Kaingang and the Guarani (Mbya).
sum: The Xetá are an Indigenous people of the Serra dos Dourados in northwestern Paraná, southern Brazil. They speak a Tupi-Guarani language.
